links.outcome: Expert-rated factuality, relevance, comprehensiveness of bariatric surgery answers with vs without the retrieval-augmented framework
links.effect: Improved quality across all five base models (p < 0.001); Cohen's d 0.96-1.01 for higher-capacity models, 0.38-0.56 for smaller; gains of +1.84 points in Risks and Complications.
links.quote: bRAGgen significantly improved response quality across all five base language models tested (p < 0.001), with large effect sizes for higher-capacity models (Cohen's d = 0.96-1.01) and moderate effects for smaller models (Cohen's d = 0.38-0.56) with good inter-rater reliability (Krippendorff's α = 0.72).

unlisted_practices: Temporal anchoring of model inference to separate stable from evolving clinical knowledge
LLM-as-Judge automated evaluation validated against expert ratings

screen.reason: The study tests the impact of adding a multi-module retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) framework with temporal anchoring onto several base LLMs to improve factuality and reduce hallucinations for bariatric patient education, evaluated via expert clinical ratings and LLM-as-judge.
